items.text: The `parse()` function in `src/index.ts` tolerates leading and trailing whitespace (fixed 2026-11-03, commit subject "fix: tolerate leading and trailing whitespace in parse()"): previously it returned NaN for whitespace-padded values such as `' 2d'` or `'1.5h '`, which commonly come from YAML configs. The fix added `\s*` at the start and end of the regex on line 84; `' 2d'` now gives 172800000 and `'1.5h '` gives 5400000. A test `should tolerate leading and trailing whitespace` is in `src/parse.test.ts`, and the change was committed as `4ae7370` on `feat/compound-format`. Caveat: the 100-character length check still counts padding, so over-padded values throw instead of returning NaN.

The short formatter in `src/index.ts` has a `compound` option, implemented via a `fmtCompound` helper, with tests in `src/format.test.ts` and a README "Compound output" section. It was added on 2026-11-03 and committed as `79e83ad` (`feat: add compound option to short formatter`) on `feat/compound-format`. The pre-commit hook passed and the branch has not been pushed. As implemented, `format(5400000, { compound: true })` returns `1h 30m`. Rules: largest unit first, zero parts skipped, parts joined by a space, units from days down to seconds (no weeks, months or years), leftover milliseconds dropped, and negative values get a leading `-`. Edge cases the agent chose without user specification: values over 30 days stay in days (40 days gives `40d`); sub-second values, positive or negative, return `0s`; if both `compound` and `long` are set, `compound` wins and output stays short form. Revised later on 2026-11-03: a separate conversation decided compound output must be Go `time.ParseDuration`-compatible, with no spaces between parts and hours as the largest unit (e.g. `25h30m`), replacing the `1d 1h 30m` style. Reason: a Go service scraping deploy logs runs every duration through `time.ParseDuration`, which rejects spaces and has no `d` unit. The user deferred that change, so it remains open and the committed implementation still uses the space-separated, days-based format.

On 2026-11-03 a feature was added: a `compound` option for the short formatter; format(5400000, { compound: true }) returns "1h 30m" (largest unit first, zero parts skipped, days to seconds, leftover ms dropped). | When: 2026-11-03 | Involving: Bench User

items.text: Early ms history (2012–2013): the `ms` repository began with an initial import on 2012-03-07. In early September 2012 TJ Holowaychuk built out core functionality (ms string support, seconds/minutes/hours/days support, ms(number) test refactor, more input flexibility, component.json), with releases 0.2.0 (2012-09-03) and 0.3.0 (2012-09-07). In late 2012 ms.js was made usable as a component (Arpad Borsos), rounding was added to fix crazy decimals (0.4.0), short formatting became the default with a `.long` option (0.5.0, 2012-11-09), and a license was added closing #18. In 2013 releases 0.5.1, 0.6.0 (2013-03-15), 0.6.1 and 0.6.2 shipped, including the fix for #22 (minutes not working due to a badly named variable) and singularization fixes with failing tests added first.
